results.why: K23 scores density of mathematical symbols, equations, notation and formulas, which is the same surface count T01 asks for, with the same explicit disclaimer about not judging the mathematics.

K15's enumerated cues (theorem references, proofs, convergence claims, bounds, regret rates, complexity statements) track T02's own gloss for learning-theory/optimization membership almost item for item, though K15 is a cue-density read rather than a topic-membership read and would give partial credit to any notation-heavy non-theory abstract.

K12 scores exactly the submission-time boilerplate T03 names — anonymised/placeholder artifact URLs plus future-tense release promises, weighted by prominence — and K48 counts the same anonymous-repo and release-upon-acceptance language; K11 is excluded because it deliberately inverts polarity (live link high, promise low) and K24 scores placeholder residue as a rush marker rather than availability boilerplate, while K07/K22 are generic availability signaling that credits ordinary live links T03 would not.

No candidate scores passive-voice grammatical construction; K08 is the nearest neighbour but contrasts first-person process narration with result-first framing, both of which are active-voice patterns.

K40 targets the same non-idiomatic-English texture (agreement errors, dropped articles, odd prepositions, misspellings) but yokes it to a required co-occurring ornate-diction component, so plain-but-error-ridden prose would score high on T05 and only middling on K40.

No candidate counts efficiency register (efficient, lightweight, scalable, low-cost); the promotional-wording items K32, K44 and K46 enumerate novelty and impact vocabulary instead, and K29/K42 score implied compute scale rather than efficiency words.

K50 and K03 are the nearest but pool named models together with benchmarks, datasets and baselines and key on prestige or lineage, so an abstract naming only ImageNet and CIFAR scores high on them and zero on T07's checkpoint-enumeration count.

No candidate scores applied-domain framing directly; K31 is the closest but is an inverted and much broader crowdedness axis whose low pole also contains classical statistics and optimization, and K49 scores urgency/impact register rather than domain membership.
No candidate mentions quotation marks or scare-quoting; K28 covers bold/italic/markup emphasis, a different attention-directing device.
K04 is priority-claim rhetoric and scores the same first-ness/record/novelty assertions T10 asks for, with the same instruction to ignore whether the claim is true.

Both count the novelty self-description lexicon at T11's core (novel, new, first), but each also folds in performance superlatives (outperforms, superior, comprehensive, robust) that T11 excludes, so scores would diverge on results-boastful abstracts that never claim novelty.
K28 scores exactly the emphasis practice T12 names — bold, italics, markdown and LaTeX emphasis markup — with the same instruction not to judge whether the emphasis helps.
